archetype.name: Playoff Team (offense-carried)
archetype.definition: A Josh Allen offense and a dominant run-blocking front good enough to win shootouts, paired with a defense playing like a bottom-five unit, so the margin for error is thinner than 3-1 suggests.

report.headline: Elite offense, leaky defense, and the 3-1 record is about what the play deserves
report.take:
Buffalo under first-year head coach Joe Brady looks like the offense of recent seasons with a sharper edge on the ground. The Bills lead the league at 31.8 points per game and rank 3rd in offensive EPA, and the run game is the clearest change. They rank 1st in stuff rate, yards before contact and run success, and they are running more than expected (pass rate over expectation -3, 21st). Allen still powers a top-five pass game. Brady has gone for it on every fourth-down chance that met the model's threshold. This offense is built to score on anyone.

The defense is the problem. Buffalo allowed between 17 and 21.6 points per game from 2021 to 2025, ranking 12th or better in defensive EPA each year. This year it is 30th in EPA allowed and 28th against the pass, allows the 27th-worst explosive pass rate, and misses tackles at the 27th-worst rate. The pass rush is fine: 8th in pressure rate, 5th in hit rate. What breaks down is coverage and finishing plays behind it. The opponents make it worse. Houston (20th in offense today) scored 31, and New England (22nd) scored 29 to hand Buffalo its loss. Only the 31st-ranked Chargers were held down.

The headline offensive numbers are softer than they look. The 36 and 41-point games came against Houston and Detroit, whose defenses rank 25th and 32nd today. Against the 11th and 12th-ranked units (LAC, NE), Buffalo scored 24 and 26, had a negative passing EPA in one of them, and turned it over seven times across the two games. That is still a good offense, just not a 32-point-a-game one. The record itself is honest: 0.34 wins over expected and a +5 per-game point differential fit a 3-1 team. Net EPA ranks 10th, not top-four as in each of the last four seasons.

Where this goes depends on the secondary. CB Christian Benford, a 91%-snap starter, is out, and nickel options Dee Alford and Te'Cory Couch are banged up. The defense was already losing in coverage at full strength. The AFC East looks soft beyond New England, with Miami 0-4 and the Jets 1-3, so a division title and double-digit wins are still the likeliest path. Beating the Kansas City, Baltimore and Chicago tier will take a defense that gets off the field.

strengths.title: League-best run blocking
strengths.body: Buffalo ranks 1st in stuff rate, yards before contact and run success, and 4th in yards per carry. That is line-driven production, not game script, and it showed most against Detroit's 203 rushing yards. Blocking success like this tends to hold up because it doesn't rely on explosive plays or turnovers.

strengths.title: Allen's efficient, aggressive passing game
strengths.body: The pass offense ranks 5th in EPA even with a run-leaning call sheet. The new staff has gone for it on 100% of fourth-down chances that met the model's threshold. The production is spread across Shakir, Moore, Kincaid and Coleman, so no single injury caps it. Pass efficiency has ranked top-four for years in this building, so it should last.

strengths.title: Pass rush is getting home
strengths.body: The front ranks 8th in pressure rate and 5th in QB hit rate with 10 sacks. That gives the defense a real tool even while the coverage struggles. With Ed Oliver questionable and T.J. Sanders out, the interior depth behind it is thinning.

concerns.title: Coverage and tackling are failing
concerns.body: Buffalo ranks 28th in pass EPA allowed and 27th in explosive pass rate allowed, and it misses tackles at the 27th-worst rate. Pressure isn't the issue, so the breakdowns are on the back end. Benford, a 91%-snap starting corner, is out, which makes it worse in the short term. This is a real flaw, not noise: mediocre offenses have already scored 29-31 points on this group.

concerns.title: Offense padded by two bad defenses
concerns.body: 77 of the 127 points came against Houston and Detroit, whose defenses rank 25th and 32nd today. Against the two top-12 defenses they faced, the offense scored 24 and 26 points and turned it over seven times, including five against the Chargers. A -0.5 turnover margin per game means the scoring rate is likely to come down from 31.8.

concerns.title: Red zone and possession leaks
concerns.body: Opponents score touchdowns on 68.8% of red-zone trips (24th), and Buffalo ranks 29th in time of possession. That partly reflects a quick-scoring offense, but it also reflects a defense that can't end drives. Tired defenders and short-field turnovers compound each other.

trend.note: Scoring dropped from 36 and 41 points against weak defenses to 24 and 26 against competent ones, with seven turnovers in those two games. The defense allowed 31, 31, 16 and 29, so it never stabilized, and the NE loss was the first non-cover.

nextGame.headline: Best defense Buffalo has seen, with a depleted secondary
nextGame.body:
The Rams are the profile that should worry this offense. They rank 4th in defensive EPA, 4th against the pass and 1st in both deep-pass EPA and explosive pass rate allowed, and they allow just 248.5 yards a game. Their weakness is the pass rush, 26th in pressure rate. Allen should have time, but he'll have to win underneath and move the ball methodically, which is how Buffalo's line wants to play anyway. On the other side, the Rams move the ball (418.3 yards per game, 2nd) but score only 21.3 points per game. A -1.3 turnover margin and 30th-ranked special teams explain much of that gap, and both are likely to improve over time.

Availability cuts both ways. Buffalo is without Benford and DT T.J. Sanders, with Oliver, Alford and DJ Moore questionable. That is a thin secondary facing Stafford behind a line that ranks 4th in pressure rate allowed. The Rams are missing Myles Garrett (IR) and CB Jaylen Watson, plus both tight ends Colby Parkinson and Terrance Ferguson. Aaron Donald is listed out with a back issue, but McVay says it is trending toward him playing.

keyMatchups.title: Allen versus a no-explosives secondary
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo's 5th-ranked pass offense meets the league's stingiest defense on deep and explosive passes. With Garrett out and the Rams' pressure rate 26th, Allen gets clean pockets but few chunk plays. Patience and red-zone execution decide this matchup.

keyMatchups.title: Buffalo's ground game sets the terms
keyMatchups.body: The Bills' 3rd-ranked run EPA faces a Rams run defense that is good but not elite, 10th in rush EPA allowed. Sustained drives would also hide a Buffalo defense that ranks 29th in time of possession. Donald's status matters most here.

keyMatchups.title: Stafford against a thin back end
keyMatchups.body: The Rams pass more than expected (6th) and protect well. Buffalo allows the 27th-worst explosive pass rate and is down its top corner. The Rams' own receiving corps is thinned at tight end, which blunts some of that edge.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Rams' turnover and special-teams leaks keep handing Buffalo short fields, since that is the clearest path for the Bills to outscore an offense that otherwise moves the ball well.

restOfSeason.body:
The run blocking and Allen's efficiency are sustainable, but 31.8 points per game isn't. The schedule includes Las Vegas (2nd-ranked defense), Minnesota (1st) and Chicago (5th), and the offense has already scored in the mid-20s against good defenses. Expect high-20s scoring. The defense should improve modestly from 30th when Benford returns, given this unit's track record of ranking 12th or better. It is unlikely to get back to that level this year with the coverage and tackling problems it has shown.

Four games against Miami (0-4) and the Jets (1-3), whose offenses rank 30th and 13th, are the floor of the season. The division title runs through New England, who already beat them. The KC, BAL, CHI and MIN games will decide seeding, and Buffalo will likely need to win those through shootouts.
swingFactors: Benford's return and the health of the secondary
Ball security after 7 turnovers in Weeks 3-4
Results against KC, BAL and CHI

bets.reason: The number looks set off Buffalo's 31.8 points per game, which was inflated by the 25th and 32nd-ranked defenses; against top-12 units the Bills scored 24 and 26. The Rams allow the fewest explosive passes in the league and score only 21.3 points per game themselves. Buffalo's porous defense is the risk to the under.

Net EPA has the Rams slightly ahead (9th vs 10th), and they are the luckless side (-0.51 wins over expected), so a home field-sized spread looks fair. Buffalo's 75% cover rate is a four-game sample and shouldn't move the number.

confidence.note: Four-game sample against a lopsided schedule, and key injuries hit both secondaries.
